grades.quote: The stimecmp register contains a time at which the the CPU will raise a timer interrupt; setting stimecmp to the current value of time plus _x_ will schedule an interrupt _x_ time units in the future.
grades.reason: Describes the analogous supervisor-level mechanism (time and stimecmp, rewriting stimecmp to schedule the next interrupt). It does not cover machine-mode mtime/mtimecmp or how the machine timer interrupt becomes pending or is cleared. Limited auxiliary value.

grades.quote: The implementation must provide a facility for scheduling timer interrupts in terms of the real-time counter, `time` .
grades.reason: Only says an implementation must provide a facility for scheduling timer interrupts in terms of the `time` counter. It does not mention mtimecmp or the pending/clear condition for the machine timer interrupt.
The mcause table only identifies the machine timer interrupt as exception code 7. It says nothing about how mtime and mtimecmp make it pending or clear it.

grades.quote: The `time` CSR is a read-only shadow of the memory-mapped `mtime` register.
grades.reason: Shows how software writes the 64-bit mtimecmp comparand without it transiently going below the old or new value. This implies a comparison against mtime. It also says the time CSR shadows mtime. The excerpt never states that the interrupt is pending when mtime >= mtimecmp, or that writing mtimecmp clears it.
